groups.title: Wildfire rescue
groups.note: RescueEnv · stored episodes run by language models
groups.method: Read from the stored episode: every drone's position after every second time step, every assignment and the share of victims rescued after every time step. Rebuilt from the seed, exactly as the episode had it: the map, the fire and the victim sites. Reconstructed by the mission's own rule from the stored positions: how many victims wait at each site.

groups.title: Choosing a nest site
groups.note: NatureEnv · bee design and a coordinator
groups.method: Run for this page by the model-free policy of the bee design; no language model is called. Each round is shown as four moments: scouts on the swarm, at the cavities, inspecting, and back on the swarm with their dances.

groups.title: Foraging and competition
groups.note: NatureEnv · patches that run out, renew and are contested
groups.method: Run for this page by the model-free policy of each design; no language model is called. Every time step of the run is a frame; a forager's place follows from the start, the length and the destination of its trip. Flowers show the loads a patch has left; arrows are advertisements at the nest, glowing lines are marks that fade.

groups.title: Trails between nest and food

groups.method: Run for this page by the model-free policy of the ant design; no language model is called. Every time step of the run is a frame; an ant's place on its path follows from the start and the length of its trip.

groups.title: Birds on migration
groups.note: NatureEnv · stored language-model episodes, and an illustration
groups.method: An illustration in the migration world of NatureEnv, not a design of the paper and not a result: every bird steers by the standard model of collective motion with its three mechanisms. The world, the hawks and which birds know the way are the mission's.

groups.title: Harder missions (held-out)
groups.note: NatureEnv · obstacles and risk · stored language-model episodes
groups.method: Stored episodes of the harder held-out missions, run by a language model after the main study. The mission is run again for this page with every reply taken from the stored decision log (no model is called), so the picture follows the stored episode step by step; the replay must end with the stored result or the page is not written.

episodes.name: Lying scouts: coordinator against bee design
episodes.about: NatureEnv mission nest-k7-liars (seven cavities; two scripted scouts never inspect and praise the poorest cavity every round), 10 agents per team. The coordinator against the bee design, every team run by Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite: stored episodes, seed 4, of seeds 0 to 5 the one whose scores lie closest to each design's mean over the seeds. Two scripted scouts praise cavity B, the poorest, in every round. The coordinator chose cavity B in round 2 (the one the liars praise); the bee design chose cavity D in round 5.
episodes.method: Stored episodes run by a language model, shown round by round. Read from the stored episode: how many scouts inspected each cavity in each round, the cavity each scout preferred afterwards, and the decision. Rebuilt from the seed: the cavities, the two lying scouts and the cavity they praise. Reconstructed: which scout stands at which cavity. Arrows: scouts that prefer a cavity (bee design) or are sent to it (coordinator).

episodes.name: A path network with a blocked stretch
episodes.about: Harder held-out mission trail-maze (eight routes of 18 to 74 steps named by their two stretches, a block at time step 32, a gap of 12 steps from 64), 8 agents per team; these missions were run after the main study, on new seeds. The coordinator against the ant design, every team run by Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite: stored episodes, seed 20, of seeds 20 to 22 the one whose scores lie closest to each design's mean over the seeds. Eight routes through a branching network; a fallen branch blocks the first stretch of the two shortest at time step 32 and a gap shorter than every route opens at 64. The coordinator brought home 29 units, with 22 of its 22 later trips through the blocked stretch; the ant design brought home 25.8 units, with 17 of its 17 later trips through the blocked stretch. Over all four models and seeds the share of later trips through the blocked stretch was 0.87 for the coordinator and 0.55 for the ant design, and no team in this episode used the gap.

episodes.name: Two equally good cavities: does the swarm split?
episodes.about: Harder held-out mission nest-k12-rival (twelve cavities, the best with a twin of equal quality in the opposite direction, a cost for waiting and a split without agreement), 10 agents per team; these missions were run after the main study, on new seeds. Solitary scouts against NatureSwarm, whole-network relay, and the coordinator, every team run by Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite: stored episodes, seed 21, of seeds 20 to 22 the one whose scores lie closest to each design's mean over the seeds. Twelve cavities; the best one (cavity A) has a twin of equal quality in the opposite direction (cavity D), every round of waiting costs 5% and a swarm that has not agreed by the last round splits. The solitary scouts had not agreed by the last round and split, 2 of 10 scouts behind cavity A (score 0.12); NatureSwarm, whole-network relay, moved into cavity L in round 2 (score 0.76); the coordinator's swarm moved into cavity E in round 2 (score 0.70).
episodes.method: Stored episodes of the harder held-out missions, run by a language model after the main study and shown round by round. Read from the stored episode: how many scouts inspected each cavity in each round, the cavity each scout preferred afterwards, and the decision. Rebuilt from the seed: the twelve cavities. Reconstructed: which scout stands at which cavity. Arrows: scouts that prefer a cavity, or are sent to it by the coordinator.

episodes.name: A hunter on the rich flowers
episodes.about: Harder held-out mission forage-risk (eight patches, the two rich ones watched by a hunter), 8 agents per team; these missions were run after the main study, on new seeds. The coordinator against the ant design, every team run by Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite: stored episodes, seed 22, of seeds 20 to 22 the one whose scores lie closest to each design's mean over the seeds. Eight patches; a crab spider hunts on the two rich, conspicuous ones, where a trip fails with probability 0.4 and costs 16 time steps; the safe patches of middle quality are easy to miss. The coordinator brought home 12.6 units and lost 10 of 27 trips to the rich patches; the ant design brought home 14.7 units and lost 7 of 17 trips to the rich patches.
